# Melkor (Morgoth)

> Melkor, mightiest of the Ainur, fell from the Music into rebellion and domination.

*Valar — the first Dark Lord*

## Overview

Melkor was the greatest and most powerful of the Ainur, but his desire to rule all of creation made him the enemy of Arda.

## Identity

- **Title:** Morgoth Bauglir
- **Role:** Discord, domination, fear and corruption
- **Spouse / consort:** Unmarried
- **Familiar symbols:** Iron Crown; Angband; Silmarils
- **Kindred:** Valar

## Names and Etymology

The name **Melkor (Morgoth)** is used throughout Tolkien's published legends for this figure.
Where an alternative name is known, it is preserved here as a secondary epithet rather than treated as a separate character.

## Character and Domain

In the Ainulindalë and Valaquenta, Melkor (Morgoth) is defined less as a mortal-style personage than as a divine power: a will, office and creative theme made visible.
The sphere associated with Melkor (Morgoth) is **Discord, domination, fear and corruption**. Tolkien repeatedly presents the Valar through consorts, crafts, music, duties and the shape of their houses.

## Relationship to Middle-earth

The Valar are the Powers of the World who entered Arda after the Music of the Ainur. They oppose Melkor, preserve creation and generally act through delegated powers rather than constant direct rule.

## Selected Quotes

> Melkor, mightiest of the Ainur, fell from the Music into rebellion and domination.

*The Silmarillion, Valaquenta.*

> The Valar, the Guardians of the World, are called the Powers of the World; they are the greatest of the Ainur who came to Arda.

*The Silmarillion, Valaquenta (condensed).*

> The Music of the Ainur brought Eä into being, and into its vision the Valar entered.

*The Silmarillion, Ainulindalë (condensed).*
